subject: Clarify metering for multi-part legal docs + bulk discount tiers
messages:
From: Jillian Park <jillian.park@orchid-financial.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@orchid-financial.com
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Metering question on doc batch + discounts

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we're finalizing the SOW: our use case is high-volume ingestion of multi-part legal documents (average 12k tokens per document, often split into 3–6 attachments per case). Pricing in the SOW references per-token billing and a monthly minimum. Two things we want to be explicit about before signature:

1) How do you meter a single logical "document" that arrives as multiple attachments / API calls (we send 3 files in quick succession for the same case)? Will the context be aggregated for billing or charged per call?

2) Our finance team also needs clarity on the bulk discount tiers in the term sheet: do discounts apply to the gross token spend or to the post-rounding invoice total? Example: if we have many 12k-token items that are rounded to your "token quantum", will rounding push us into a higher tier unpredictably?

I've attached the SOW draft and a small usage snapshot for context. Can you confirm behavior and ideally include a short example we can show procurement?

Thanks,
Jillian
Jillian Park
Head of Procurement, Orchid Financial
attachments: Orchid_SOW_v3.pdf, usage_snapshot_q3.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jillian Park <jillian.park@orchid-financial.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Metering question on doc batch + discounts

Hi Jillian — thanks for the clear examples and the SOW. Short answer up front: we can treat the 3 files for a single case as a single billing "session" so long as they meet our session correlation rules (same case_id header or same top-level metadata within a 15-minute window). Ill explain below and include a worked example for procurement.

Worked example (simplified):
- Each file: ~12,000 tokens. 3 files = 36,000 total tokens.
- Our token quantum (metering granularity) = 256 tokens. We round each session total to the nearest quantum (round up). 36,000 / 256 = 140.625 -> rounded = 141 quanta -> billed tokens = 141 * 256 = 36,096 tokens.
- Discounts: tiering applies to the billed token total (post-quantum rounding) for the invoice period. So your shipment would be counted as 36,096 tokens toward the monthly consumption that maps to the discount slab.

Notes / options: if you prefer the rounding per-call instead of session-aggregation we can also do that (we default to session-aggregation when correlation metadata is present). Per-call rounding would result in slightly higher billed tokens in this example.

I'll loop in Marcus for a quick check on how this interacts with the committed-tier discount math and whether we'd offer a rounding cap for predictable tiering.

- Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: internal: ORCH-295 rounding/tier behavior + concession ask

Kimberly / Marissa — quick internal note so we're aligned before I reply to Jillian:

1) Confirming Kimberly's math above; session-aggregation with a 15-minute correlation window and case_id metadata gives the cleanest result for customers who batch parts of the same document. We should include that as a recommended practice in the SOW (metadata header example).

2) Discount tiers: Orchid is near the threshold between the 10% and 12% tiers for committed monthly volume. If post-rounding usage pushes them over the threshold in a month, that works in their favor; the concern is small rounding steps pushing them *below* a threshold unpredictably.

3) Suggested concession to close: offer a monthly rounding buffer (cap) of up to 0.5% of billed tokens for the first three billing cycles. If rounding-induced variance exceeds that, offer a one-time credit to bring them to the expected tier. This preserves economics while removing procurement friction.

4) Legal / billing ops note: if we include the buffer in the SOW, we need language limiting repeated abuse and defining how we measure "same-case" correlation (case_id or same customer-request-id). Also need Finance sign-off on the credit process (marissa).

Marissa — can you sanity-check the 0.5% cap and confirm Finance is OK with handling credits up to that amount administratively (without exec signoff)? If not, what's the upper bound you can approve?

- Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jillian Park <jillian.park@orchid-financial.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 15:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Metering question on doc batch + discounts

Jillian / Marcus / Kimberly — thanks for the helpful thread. Finance has reviewed the proposed approach.

Decision summary for SOW language (for procurement/legal):
- Session aggregation: Redwood will aggregate calls that include the same customer_request_id or case_id within a 15-minute window and bill the aggregated token total rounded up to our 256-token quantum.
- Tiering: Discounts are applied to the billed token total for the invoice period (post-rounding).
- Rounding buffer: Redwood will apply a one-time monthly rounding buffer up to 0.5% of billed tokens for the first three months after go-live. If the monthly rounding variance exceeds 0.5%, Redwood will issue a single credit to reconcile to the expected tier for that month. The buffer is intended to protect customers during ramp and is not a standing credit thereafter.

Next steps for you: if Orchid is comfortable, we'll add this paragraph to the SOW and append a short correlation header example (x-case-id in request metadata). We'll also include an example table (your 3 x 12k file case) so procurement can see the math.

Jillian — happy to add this text to the SOW and re-send for signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
